findings.defect: pollUntil treats every non-ok read-back response as 'not found yet' and keeps polling, so an authentication or path error on the consumer endpoint is reported as a propagation timeout.
findings.failureScenario: GET_READY_TOKEN expired (401) or the read-back path wrong (404): the loop burns the full timeoutSeconds, then fails with 'get-ready never reflected taskId within 30s' — indistinguishable from CDC never delivering — so a credential problem is triaged as a broken flow and the real cause is hidden.
findings.evidence: packages/functest/src/emit.ts:153-159 'const res = await fetch(opts.url, …); if (res.ok) { … }' with no else branch and :187 the only failure message; contrast the conformance emitter which asserts res.ok with the status (packages/testgen/src/emit.ts:47). Rule: R-117b.

verification.reason: A non-ok read-back response falls through the `if (res.ok)` block with no else branch, so a 401/404 is retried until the deadline and the only failure surfaced is the propagation-timeout message at line 187; unlike the conformance emitter, nothing asserts res.ok or records res.status for the read-back.

findings.defect: When none of several referenced entities is groundable, ground() falls back to referenced[0] — the alphabetically-first mention — so the recorded skip reason can name an incidental single-source entity instead of the requirement's cross-service subject.
findings.failureScenario: A requirement that mentions both ResultPackage (two sources, unmapped) and CdcEnvelope (one source) is skipped as "single-service entity 'CdcEnvelope' (no cross-service counterpart)" although the entity it is about is ResultPackage and the R-121 reason that applies is "no API mapping for entity 'ResultPackage'"; a reader triaging skips by reason is sent to the wrong entity and the wrong fix (declare a flow vs add an API mapping).
findings.evidence: packages/functest/src/ground.ts:113 entities sorted, :121-127 'const entity = groundable ?? referenced[0];' after the groundable find() fails; the doc comment at :99-102 says grounding 'picks the referenced entity with an API mapping' and :121-122 'report the most specific reason', which the fallback does not do. Rule: R-121.

verification.reason: referenced is derived from a code-point-sorted entity list and, when no entity is both cross-service and mapped, the fallback is referenced[0]; with CdcEnvelope (single-source) and ResultPackage (two sources, unmapped) both mentioned, 'CdcEnvelope' sorts first and the skip reason becomes the single-service one rather than ResultPackage's no-API-mapping reason. The comment at lines 119-120 shows this fallback is intentional ('for the first referenced entity'), so it is documented design rather than an accident, but the behaviour the finding describes is real.
